newsitem.title: JAPAN: Crudes up in Asia, Minas seen firm on wet market.
newsitem.headline: Crudes up in Asia, Minas seen firm on wet market.

text.p: Crude prices were firm to strong in Asia on Thursday, buoyed by bullish market sentiment, despite an absence of fresh, strong incentives, traders said.
Premiums for Minas firmed in the wet market, pulling up indications for some other crudes such as Bach Ho. However active players were conspicuously absent from the market.
"Prices are too high, and I think that's why the (wet) market's quiet," one trader said.
January cash Brent was notionally assessed at $23.90/23.40, compared with late U.S. quotes of $23.80/23.90.

In spreads, Brent/Dubai was notionally assessed at $1.90/1.95 for January, February and March, little changed from overnight late-U.S. levels. In the Dubai paper market, a February/March Dubai changed hands at plus 60 cents.
In the wet market, trading in Gulf crudes appeared to be pausing ahead of the next active trading month.

In regional crudes, a producer was offering January Tapis at a premium of $1.10 above industry quotes after the latest deal done at $1.00. The producer was negotiating with Thailand on some cargoes, with bids at a premium of 80-90 cents.
Paper Tapis quotes were at around $23.80.

Traders said two Australian crudes were believed traded. A 700,000-barrel cargo of Cossack was believed sold by a major to Thailand at 25 cents above industry quotes, while a Challis was believed to have exchanged hands at a premium of $1.50.

January Minas appeared to be looking up, buoyed by demand anticipated from Japanese electric utility companies covering winter requirements. Minas was assessed fetching a premium of about ICP plus 45 cents. January Bach Ho was also believed firming, with two recent deals widely believed done at around 40 to 45 cents above the official selling price, more than double the premium of last deals done for the crude.
